<!--
  Analysis code for the manuscript on sensory impairment, frailty, and incident
  dementia in the HRS (United States) and ELSA (England) cohorts.

  DATA NOT INCLUDED. HRS and ELSA are restricted-access and cannot be
  redistributed. Obtain the source data from the data providers and place them
  under data/ (git-ignored) so the relative paths in this notebook resolve.
  See README.md for setup and run order.
-->

<!--
ELSA counterpart of HRS_analysis_Cox.Rmd. Same cohort rules, interval
construction, models, PAF method, sensitivity analyses and saved outputs.
The two setup chunks below ("Shared setup" and "Load data") are identical
in ELSA_analysis_Cox.Rmd and ELSA_analysis_MSM.Rmd.

Differences from HRS, all because of the ELSA data:
  * No death tracking and no Fine-Gray competing-risk analysis (ELSA has
    no usable mortality data).
  * Follow-up ends at the last ELSA wave in elsa_long.csv, 2018 (HRS: 2020).
  * Attained-age time scale from calendar years: age at each wave = wave
    year - birth year (no interview or birth month in the ELSA End User
    Licence files). HRS uses age in months from the interview dates.
  * Reduced frailty index derived from the 36-item noIADL counts plus the
    CES-D items read from the core files (built in ELSA_extractdata.Rmd).
  * Every saved file ends in _ELSA instead of _HRS.
ELSA variable names: idauniq (id), frailty (HRS Frailty_status), fi_score
(HRS FI_score).
-->


# Shared setup: libraries, data load, cohort construction
```{r}
library(haven)
library(dplyr)
library(labelled)
library(tidyverse)
library(stringr)
library(lubridate)
library(msm)
library(survival)
library(survminer)
library(scales)
```


# Load data
```{r}
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Paths are relative to the REPOSITORY ROOT, not to code/.
#
# RStudio runs .Rmd chunks with the working directory set to the notebook's own
# folder, so without this the code would look for code/data/ instead of data/.
# The root is resolved into a variable rather than with setwd(), because a
# setwd() inside a chunk does not persist to the next chunk.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
repo_root <- if (basename(getwd()) == "code") normalizePath("..") else normalizePath(".")
cat("Repository root:", repo_root, "\n")
data_dir    <- file.path(repo_root, "data")      # harmonised person-wave data (input)
results_dir <- file.path(repo_root, "results")   # model output: tables (.csv) and fits (.rds)
output_dir  <- file.path(repo_root, "output")    # figures
dir.create(results_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
dir.create(output_dir,  showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

elsa_long_path <- file.path(data_dir, "elsa_long.csv")
ELSA_long <- read_csv(
  elsa_long_path,
  guess_max = Inf,                          # rows are stacked by wave; guess types from all of them
  col_types = cols(
    idauniq = col_character(),
    year    = col_integer(),
    .default = col_guess()
  )
)
stopifnot(nrow(problems(ELSA_long)) == 0)   # any parsing failure stops here
stopifnot(nrow(count(ELSA_long, idauniq, year) %>% filter(n > 1)) == 0)

baseline_start <- 2002L
baseline_end   <- 2008L

# 0) Apply cummax to dementia — make it irreversible
#    Same rule as HRS: a wave without a dementia assessment stays NA unless
#    dementia was already observed at an earlier wave.
ELSA_long_fixed <- ELSA_long %>%
  arrange(idauniq, year) %>%
  group_by(idauniq) %>%
  mutate(
    dementia_observed = as.integer(dementia),
    ever_dementia     = cummax(coalesce(dementia_observed, 0L)),
    dementia = case_when(
      ever_dementia == 1L       ~ 1L,
      !is.na(dementia_observed) ~ dementia_observed,
      TRUE                      ~ NA_integer_
    )
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(-dementia_observed, -ever_dementia) %>%
  ungroup()

revert_check <- ELSA_long_fixed %>%
  arrange(idauniq, year) %>%
  group_by(idauniq) %>%
  mutate(reverted = !is.na(lag(dementia)) & lag(dementia) == 1 & dementia == 0) %>%
  ungroup()
cat("Reversions remaining after cummax():", sum(revert_check$reverted, na.rm = TRUE), "\n")

cat("\nDementia person-waves after cummax:",
    sum(ELSA_long_fixed$dementia == 1, na.rm = TRUE), "\n")
cat("Unique dementia people:",
    n_distinct(ELSA_long_fixed$idauniq[ELSA_long_fixed$dementia == 1]), "\n")

cat("\nPerson-waves with unknown dementia status (NA) after carry-forward:",
    sum(is.na(ELSA_long_fixed$dementia)), "\n")

n_never_assessed <- ELSA_long_fixed %>%
  group_by(idauniq) %>%
  summarise(all_na = all(is.na(dementia)), .groups = "drop") %>%
  summarise(n = sum(all_na)) %>%
  pull(n)
cat("People never assessed for dementia in any wave:", n_never_assessed, "\n")

# 1) Identify baseline year per person
#    Require: age >= 50, dementia == 0, hearing_loss, vision_overall, frailty not missing
baseline_tbl <- ELSA_long_fixed %>%
  filter(year >= baseline_start, year <= baseline_end) %>%
  filter(!is.na(age), age >= 50) %>%
  filter(!is.na(dementia), dementia == 0) %>%
  filter(!is.na(hearing_loss)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(vision_overall)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(frailty)) %>%
  group_by(idauniq) %>%
  summarise(baseline_year = min(year), .groups = "drop")

cat("\nParticipants with valid baseline:", nrow(baseline_tbl), "\n")

# 2) Extract the baseline row (one per person)
baseline_df <- ELSA_long_fixed %>%
  inner_join(baseline_tbl, by = "idauniq") %>%
  filter(year == baseline_year) %>%
  distinct(idauniq, .keep_all = TRUE)

# 3) Build panel: baseline + all follow-up waves
panel_df <- ELSA_long_fixed %>%
  inner_join(baseline_tbl, by = "idauniq") %>%
  filter(year >= baseline_year)

# 4) Eligibility: ≥2 valid waves on each measure; has follow-up
eligible_ids <- panel_df %>%
  group_by(idauniq) %>%
  summarise(
    n_rounds         = n(),
    n_hearing_valid  = sum(!is.na(hearing_loss)),
    n_vision_valid   = sum(!is.na(vision_overall)),
    n_frailty_valid  = sum(!is.na(frailty)),
    n_dementia_valid = sum(!is.na(dementia)),
    has_fu           = any(year > baseline_year),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  filter(
    n_rounds         >= 2,
    n_hearing_valid  >= 2,
    n_vision_valid   >= 2,
    n_frailty_valid  >= 2,
    n_dementia_valid >= 2,
    has_fu
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(idauniq)

baseline_df_eligible <- baseline_df %>%
  semi_join(eligible_ids, by = "idauniq")

panel_df_eligible <- panel_df %>%
  semi_join(eligible_ids, by = "idauniq")

cat("\nFinal eligible participants:", nrow(baseline_df_eligible), "\n")
cat("Final person-waves:", nrow(panel_df_eligible), "\n")

```


# Cox models (model 1,2,3,4) for hearing loss and vision loss (ELSA)

```{r}
library(survival)

# Last ELSA wave in elsa_long.csv (wave 9, 2018). HRS uses 2020, its last
# wave with dementia ascertainment.
last_wave <- 2018L

# Time-invariant covariates from baseline (includes baseline age)
baseline_invariant <- baseline_df_eligible %>%
  mutate(idauniq = as.character(idauniq)) %>%
  dplyr::select(idauniq, Gender, Race, Education, Marital_status, age) %>%
  rename(baseline_age = age)

df0_all <- panel_df_eligible %>%
  mutate(idauniq = as.character(idauniq)) %>%
  dplyr::select(-Gender, -Race, -Education, -Marital_status) %>%
  left_join(baseline_invariant, by = "idauniq") %>%
  mutate(
    year          = as.integer(year),
    baseline_year = as.integer(baseline_year),
    time          = as.numeric(year - baseline_year),

    # outcome (binary)
    dementia       = as.integer(dementia),

    # binary exposures stay integer 0/1
    hearing_loss   = as.integer(hearing_loss),
    vision_overall = as.integer(vision_overall),
    frailty = as.integer(frailty),

    # categorical exposures/covariates -> factors
    Employment     = factor(Employment),
    Smoking        = factor(Smoking),
    Alcohol        = factor(Alcohol),
    Gender         = factor(Gender),
    Race           = factor(Race),
    Education      = factor(Education),
    Marital_status = factor(Marital_status),

    baseline_age   = as.numeric(baseline_age)
  ) %>%
  arrange(idauniq, time)

# Waves with an assessed dementia status (should stop at 2018)
cat("Waves with assessed dementia status:\n")
print(table(df0_all$year[!is.na(df0_all$dementia)]))

# Persons with an unassessed wave before their last assessed wave. These
# waves are skipped below, so follow-up continues to the next assessed wave
# instead of stopping at the first missing dementia status.
na_gap <- df0_all %>%
  group_by(idauniq) %>%
  summarise(
    first_na  = suppressWarnings(min(time[is.na(dementia)])),
    last_obs  = max(time[!is.na(dementia)]),
    dem_after = any(dementia == 1 & time > first_na, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
cat("Persons with an unassessed wave before their last assessed wave:",
    sum(na_gap$first_na < na_gap$last_obs),
    " | dementia events after such a wave:", sum(na_gap$dem_after), "\n")

# Keep assessed waves only, within the MSM window (waves up to 2018).
# An interval then runs from one assessed wave to the next assessed wave;
# exposures still come from the start of that interval.
df0 <- df0_all %>%
  filter(!is.na(dementia), year <= last_wave)

# 1) Build interval dataset (counting-process format)
tv_dat <- df0 %>%
  group_by(idauniq) %>%
  mutate(
    tstart      = lag(time),
    tstop       = time,
    event       = dementia,

    # status at the START of the interval
    hearing_lag = lag(hearing_loss),
    vision_lag  = lag(vision_overall),
    frailty_lag = lag(frailty),

    emp_lag     = lag(Employment),
    smoke_lag   = lag(Smoking),
    alcohol_lag = lag(Alcohol)
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  filter(!is.na(tstart), tstop > tstart)

# 2) Keep intervals up to first dementia event
tv_dat <- tv_dat %>%
  group_by(idauniq) %>%
  mutate(event_cum = cumsum(event)) %>%
  filter(event_cum <= 1) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  dplyr::select(-event_cum)

stopifnot(!anyNA(tv_dat$event))

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3) Common analytic sample (complete-case on the M4 covariate set)
#    Using the same rows for M1-M4 makes HRs across models comparable.
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
tv_cc <- tv_dat %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(hearing_lag), !is.na(vision_lag), !is.na(frailty_lag),
    !is.na(emp_lag),    !is.na(smoke_lag),  !is.na(alcohol_lag),
    !is.na(baseline_age),
    !is.na(Gender), !is.na(Race), !is.na(Education), !is.na(Marital_status)
  )

# Report what the complete-case restriction costs
cat("Before CC  -> intervals:", nrow(tv_dat),
    " | persons:", dplyr::n_distinct(tv_dat$idauniq),
    " | events:", sum(tv_dat$event), "\n")
cat("Analytic intervals:", nrow(tv_cc),
    " | unique persons:", dplyr::n_distinct(tv_cc$idauniq),
    " | events:", sum(tv_cc$event), "\n")

# ======================================================================
# Helper: tidy HR table
# ======================================================================
tidy_hr <- function(fit, terms = NULL, model_label = NA_character_) {
  out <- broom::tidy(fit, exponentiate = TRUE, conf.int = TRUE) %>%
    dplyr::select(term, HR = estimate, conf.low, conf.high, p.value) %>%
    mutate(
      HR_CI = sprintf("%.2f (%.2f-%.2f)", HR, conf.low, conf.high),
      model = model_label
    )
  if (!is.null(terms)) out <- out %>% filter(term %in% terms)
  out
}

# Helper: print intervals / persons / events for each fit
fit_n <- function(fit, label, data = tv_cc, id = "idauniq") {
  cat(sprintf("[%s]  intervals = %d   persons = %d   events = %d\n",
              label, fit$n, dplyr::n_distinct(data[[id]]), fit$nevent))
}

# ======================================================================
# Pre-flight checks (exposure prevalence, correlation and VIF; Supplementary Table 35)
# ======================================================================
prev_tab <- tv_cc %>%
  count(hearing_lag, vision_lag, frailty_lag) %>%
  mutate(pct = round(100 * n / sum(n), 1))
print(prev_tab)

# Correlation among the three exposures (frailty as numeric just for diagnostics)
cor_tab <- tv_cc %>%
  mutate(frailty_num = as.numeric(frailty_lag)) %>%
  dplyr::select(hearing_lag, vision_lag, frailty_num) %>%
  cor()
print(round(cor_tab, 3))

# VIF: use a logistic GLM for a more appropriate diagnostic on a binary outcome
vif_check <- glm(
  event ~ hearing_lag + vision_lag + frailty_lag +
    baseline_age + Gender + Race + Education + Marital_status +
    emp_lag + smoke_lag + alcohol_lag,
  data = tv_cc, family = binomial()
)
print(car::vif(vif_check))

# ======================================================================
# Model 1: Unadjusted (one Cox per exposure)
# ======================================================================
fit_m1_hearing <- coxph(
  Surv(tstart, tstop, event) ~ hearing_lag + cluster(idauniq),
  data = tv_cc, ties = "efron"
)
summary(fit_m1_hearing); fit_n(fit_m1_hearing, "M1 hearing")

fit_m1_vision <- coxph(
  Surv(tstart, tstop, event) ~ vision_lag + cluster(idauniq),
  data = tv_cc, ties = "efron"
)
summary(fit_m1_vision); fit_n(fit_m1_vision, "M1 vision")

fit_m1_frailty <- coxph(
  Surv(tstart, tstop, event) ~ frailty_lag + cluster(idauniq),
  data = tv_cc, ties = "efron"
)
summary(fit_m1_frailty); fit_n(fit_m1_frailty, "M1 frailty")

# ======================================================================
# Model 2: + age
# ======================================================================
fit_m2_hearing <- coxph(
  Surv(tstart, tstop, event) ~ hearing_lag +
    baseline_age +
    cluster(idauniq),
  data = tv_cc, ties = "efron"
)
summary(fit_m2_hearing); fit_n(fit_m2_hearing, "M2 hearing")

fit_m2_vision <- coxph(
  Surv(tstart, tstop, event) ~ vision_lag +
    baseline_age +
    cluster(idauniq),
  data = tv_cc, ties = "efron"
)
summary(fit_m2_vision); fit_n(fit_m2_vision, "M2 vision")

fit_m2_frailty <- coxph(
  Surv(tstart, tstop, event) ~ frailty_lag +
    baseline_age +
    cluster(idauniq),
  data = tv_cc, ties = "efron"
)
summary(fit_m2_frailty); fit_n(fit_m2_frailty, "M2 frailty")

# ======================================================================
# Model 3: + sex, race, education, marital status,
#          employment, smoking, alcohol
# ======================================================================
fit_m3_hearing <- coxph(
  Surv(tstart, tstop, event) ~ hearing_lag +
    baseline_age + Gender + Race + Education + Marital_status +
    emp_lag + smoke_lag + alcohol_lag +
    cluster(idauniq),
  data = tv_cc, ties = "efron"
)
summary(fit_m3_hearing); fit_n(fit_m3_hearing, "M3 hearing")

fit_m3_vision <- coxph(
  Surv(tstart, tstop, event) ~ vision_lag +
    baseline_age + Gender + Race + Education + Marital_status +
    emp_lag + smoke_lag + alcohol_lag +
    cluster(idauniq),
  data = tv_cc, ties = "efron"
)
summary(fit_m3_vision); fit_n(fit_m3_vision, "M3 vision")

fit_m3_frailty <- coxph(
  Surv(tstart, tstop, event) ~ frailty_lag +
    baseline_age + Gender + Race + Education + Marital_status +
    emp_lag + smoke_lag + alcohol_lag +
    cluster(idauniq),
  data = tv_cc, ties = "efron"
)
summary(fit_m3_frailty); fit_n(fit_m3_frailty, "M3 frailty")

# ======================================================================
# Model 4 (PRIMARY): hybrid design
#   - Hearing HR  -> separate Cox (hearing  + frailty + covariates)
#   - Vision  HR  -> separate Cox (vision   + frailty + covariates)
#   - Frailty HR  -> mutually adjusted Cox (hearing + vision + frailty + covariates)
# ======================================================================

# ---- Hearing row: separate Cox, frailty as covariate -----------------------
fit_m4_hearing <- coxph(
  Surv(tstart, tstop, event) ~ hearing_lag +
    baseline_age + Gender + Race + Education + Marital_status +
    emp_lag + smoke_lag + alcohol_lag + frailty_lag +
    cluster(idauniq),
  data = tv_cc, ties = "efron"
)
summary(fit_m4_hearing); fit_n(fit_m4_hearing, "M4 hearing")
cox.zph(fit_m4_hearing)

# ---- Vision row: separate Cox, frailty as covariate ------------------------
fit_m4_vision <- coxph(
  Surv(tstart, tstop, event) ~ vision_lag +
    baseline_age + Gender + Race + Education + Marital_status +
    emp_lag + smoke_lag + alcohol_lag + frailty_lag +
    cluster(idauniq),
  data = tv_cc, ties = "efron"
)
summary(fit_m4_vision); fit_n(fit_m4_vision, "M4 vision")
cox.zph(fit_m4_vision)

# ---- Frailty row: mutually-adjusted Cox (single coherent frailty HR) -------
# Its hearing_lag / vision_lag rows can be reported as a supplementary
# mutually-adjusted result.
fit_m4_frailty <- coxph(
  Surv(tstart, tstop, event) ~
    hearing_lag + vision_lag + frailty_lag +
    baseline_age + Gender + Race + Education + Marital_status +
    emp_lag + smoke_lag + alcohol_lag +
    cluster(idauniq),
  data = tv_cc, ties = "efron"
)
summary(fit_m4_frailty); fit_n(fit_m4_frailty, "M4 frailty")
cox.zph(fit_m4_frailty)

# ======================================================================
# Model 4 + sensory x frailty interaction (Supplementary Table 34)
#   Same rows and covariates as Model 4; adds the product term.
#   Reports: interaction (ratio of HRs) with robust Wald P, sensory HR in
#   non-frail and frail intervals, and RERI (additive scale).
#   Variances come from vcov(fit) = robust (cluster) variance; do not use
#   anova() for the P value, because its LR test ignores cluster().
# ======================================================================
fit_m4_int_hearing <- coxph(
  Surv(tstart, tstop, event) ~ hearing_lag * frailty_lag +
    baseline_age + Gender + Race + Education + Marital_status +
    emp_lag + smoke_lag + alcohol_lag +
    cluster(idauniq),
  data = tv_cc, ties = "efron"
)
summary(fit_m4_int_hearing); fit_n(fit_m4_int_hearing, "M4 hearing x frailty")

fit_m4_int_vision <- coxph(
  Surv(tstart, tstop, event) ~ vision_lag * frailty_lag +
    baseline_age + Gender + Race + Education + Marital_status +
    emp_lag + smoke_lag + alcohol_lag +
    cluster(idauniq),
  data = tv_cc, ties = "efron"
)
summary(fit_m4_int_vision); fit_n(fit_m4_int_vision, "M4 vision x frailty")

# Stratum-specific HRs, interaction and RERI.
# Prints plain text with cat(), so the output does not depend on how data
# frames or tibbles display in the console.
report_int <- function(fit, exposure, label, frailty = "frailty_lag") {
  b  <- coef(fit)
  V  <- vcov(fit)                                   # robust (cluster) variance
  e  <- exposure; f <- frailty; ef <- paste0(e, ":", f)
  z  <- qnorm(0.975)

  # linear combination of coefficients -> HR, 95% CI, robust Wald P
  lc <- function(w) {
    est <- sum(w * b[names(w)])
    se  <- sqrt(drop(t(w) %*% V[names(w), names(w)] %*% w))
    c(HR = exp(est), lo = exp(est - z * se), hi = exp(est + z * se),
      p = 2 * pnorm(-abs(est / se)))
  }
  fmt_p <- function(p) if (p < 0.001) "P < 0.001" else sprintf("P = %.3f", p)
  line  <- function(name, x)
    cat(sprintf("  %-30s %.2f (%.2f-%.2f)   %s\n",
                name, x[["HR"]], x[["lo"]], x[["hi"]], fmt_p(x[["p"]])))

  nf  <- lc(setNames(1,       e))
  fr  <- lc(setNames(c(1, 1), c(e, ef)))
  int <- lc(setNames(1,       ef))

  # RERI = HR11 - HR10 - HR01 + 1 (delta method)
  h10  <- exp(b[[e]]); h01 <- exp(b[[f]]); h11 <- exp(b[[e]] + b[[f]] + b[[ef]])
  reri <- h11 - h10 - h01 + 1
  g    <- c(h11 - h10, h11 - h01, h11)
  se_r <- sqrt(drop(t(g) %*% V[c(e, f, ef), c(e, f, ef)] %*% g))

  cat("\n", label, "\n", sep = "")
  line("Sensory HR, non-frail", nf)
  line("Sensory HR, frail", fr)
  line("Interaction (ratio of HRs)", int)
  cat(sprintf("  %-30s %.2f (%.2f to %.2f)\n", "RERI",
              reri, reri - z * se_r, reri + z * se_r))

  invisible(data.frame(quantity = c("non-frail", "frail", "interaction"),
                       rbind(nf, fr, int), row.names = NULL))
}

int_hearing <- report_int(fit_m4_int_hearing, "hearing_lag", "HEARING x FRAILTY")
int_vision  <- report_int(fit_m4_int_vision,  "vision_lag",  "VISION x FRAILTY")

# Cross-check for the frail stratum: recode frailty so that "frail" is the
# reference level. The sensory main effect is then the HR among frail
# intervals, and summary() prints its robust CI and P directly. It must match
# the "Sensory HR, frail" line above.
fit_frail_ref_h <- coxph(
  Surv(tstart, tstop, event) ~ hearing_lag * I(1 - frailty_lag) +
    baseline_age + Gender + Race + Education + Marital_status +
    emp_lag + smoke_lag + alcohol_lag + cluster(idauniq),
  data = tv_cc, ties = "efron"
)
fit_frail_ref_v <- coxph(
  Surv(tstart, tstop, event) ~ vision_lag * I(1 - frailty_lag) +
    baseline_age + Gender + Race + Education + Marital_status +
    emp_lag + smoke_lag + alcohol_lag + cluster(idauniq),
  data = tv_cc, ties = "efron"
)
summary(fit_frail_ref_h)$conf.int["hearing_lag", ]
summary(fit_frail_ref_h)$coefficients["hearing_lag", ]
summary(fit_frail_ref_v)$conf.int["vision_lag", ]
summary(fit_frail_ref_v)$coefficients["vision_lag", ]

```


# Model 5 (ELSA): sensory impairment by frailty context and incident dementia
# Attendance and follow-up, ELSA (Supplementary Table 12)
```{r}
wave_step    <- 2
analytic_ids <- unique(as.character(tv_cc$idauniq))

base_status <- df0_all %>%
  mutate(idauniq = as.character(idauniq)) %>%
  filter(idauniq %in% analytic_ids, time == 0) %>%
  transmute(idauniq,
            hearing0 = factor(hearing_loss,   0:1, c("No", "Yes")),
            vision0  = factor(vision_overall, 0:1, c("No", "Yes")),
            frailty0 = factor(frailty,        0:1, c("No", "Yes")))

att_rows <- df0 %>%
  mutate(idauniq = as.character(idauniq)) %>%
  filter(idauniq %in% analytic_ids) %>%
  arrange(idauniq, time) %>%
  group_by(idauniq) %>%
  filter(cumsum(dementia) <= 1) %>%
  mutate(gap = time - lag(time)) %>%
  ungroup()

cat("Years between consecutive assessments (ELSA):\n")
print(table(att_rows$gap, useNA = "no"))

attend <- att_rows %>%
  group_by(idauniq) %>%
  summarise(
    n_assess = n(),
    fu_years = max(time),
    n_missed = max(time) / wave_step + 1 - n(),
    gap_mean = if (n() > 1) mean(gap, na.rm = TRUE) else NA_real_,
    .groups  = "drop"
  ) %>%
  left_join(base_status, by = "idauniq")

stopifnot(nrow(attend) == length(analytic_ids),
          !anyNA(attend$hearing0), !anyNA(attend$vision0), !anyNA(attend$frailty0),
          all(attend$n_missed >= 0))

mq <- function(x, d = 0) sprintf(paste0("%.", d, "f (%.", d, "f-%.", d, "f)"),
                                 median(x), quantile(x, .25), quantile(x, .75))
summ_att <- function(d) d %>% summarise(
  n                      = n(),
  assessments_median_IQR = mq(n_assess),
  followup_years_med_IQR = mq(fu_years, 1),
  mean_interval_years    = sprintf("%.2f", mean(gap_mean, na.rm = TRUE)),
  any_missed_wave_n_pct  = sprintf("%d (%.1f)", sum(n_missed > 0), 100 * mean(n_missed > 0)))
by_grp <- function(var, label) attend %>%
  group_by(level = .data[[var]]) %>% summ_att() %>%
  mutate(group = label, level = as.character(level))

att_tab_elsa <- bind_rows(
  summ_att(attend) %>% mutate(group = "Overall", level = "All"),
  by_grp("hearing0", "Hearing impairment at baseline"),
  by_grp("vision0",  "Vision impairment at baseline"),
  by_grp("frailty0", "Frailty at baseline")) %>%
  relocate(group, level)
print(att_tab_elsa)

p_tab_elsa <- bind_rows(lapply(c("hearing0", "vision0", "frailty0"), function(g) tibble(
  group      = g,
  p_assess   = wilcox.test(attend$n_assess ~ attend[[g]])$p.value,
  p_followup = wilcox.test(attend$fu_years ~ attend[[g]])$p.value,
  p_missed   = chisq.test(table(attend$n_missed > 0, attend[[g]]))$p.value)))
print(p_tab_elsa)

cat("ELSA analytic intervals longer than one wave:",
    sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * mean(tv_cc$tstop - tv_cc$tstart > wave_step)), "\n")

write.csv(att_tab_elsa, file.path(results_dir, "attendance_ELSA.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

```


```{r}
m5_labels <- function(sensory_label) {
  c(paste0("No ", sensory_label, " (ref)"),
    paste0(sensory_label, ", no frailty yet"),
    paste0(sensory_label, ", frailty present"))
}

m5_display <- c("No impairment (ref)",
                "Before frailty onset",
                "With or after frailty onset")

# ==========================================================================
# Build the Model 5 interval data
# ==========================================================================
build_m5_dataset <- function(sensory_var, sensory_lag, sensory_label,
                             interval_df = tv_cc,
                             panel_df    = panel_df_eligible,
                             frailty_var = "frailty",
                             frailty_lag = "frailty_lag") {

  # ---- 1) Onset history from every observed wave --------------------------
  # Frailty history at each wave: recorded frail at this wave or any earlier
  # one. Waves without a dementia assessment still carry real frailty and
  # sensory information, so they count towards the history.
  history <- panel_df %>%
    mutate(
      idauniq        = as.character(idauniq),
      year          = as.integer(year),
      baseline_year = as.integer(baseline_year),
      time          = as.numeric(year - baseline_year),
      .frail        = as.integer(.data[[frailty_var]]),
      .sensory      = as.integer(.data[[sensory_var]])
    ) %>%
    arrange(idauniq, time) %>%
    group_by(idauniq) %>%
    mutate(
      frail_hist = cummax(coalesce(.frail, 0L)),
      # first wave each condition was observed (used for description only;
      # an interval in category 2 has both onsets at or before its start)
      first_sensory_time = if (any(.sensory == 1, na.rm = TRUE))
                             min(time[.sensory == 1], na.rm = TRUE)
                           else NA_real_,
      first_frail_time   = if (any(.frail == 1, na.rm = TRUE))
                             min(time[.frail == 1], na.rm = TRUE)
                           else NA_real_
    ) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    dplyr::select(idauniq, start_year = year, frail_hist_start = frail_hist,
                  first_sensory_time, first_frail_time)

  # ---- 2) Classify each interval from its opening wave --------------------
  df_tv <- interval_df %>%
    mutate(
      idauniq         = as.character(idauniq),
      start          = tstart,
      stop           = tstop,
      dementia_event = as.integer(event),
      start_year     = as.integer(round(as.integer(baseline_year) + tstart)),
      sensory_start  = as.integer(.data[[sensory_lag]]),
      frail_start    = as.integer(.data[[frailty_lag]])
    ) %>%
    left_join(history, by = c("idauniq", "start_year")) %>%
    mutate(
      ctx_num = case_when(
        sensory_start == 0                         ~ 0L,
        sensory_start == 1 & frail_hist_start == 0 ~ 1L,
        sensory_start == 1 & frail_hist_start == 1 ~ 2L,
        TRUE                                       ~ NA_integer_
      ),
      ctx_lag = factor(ctx_num, levels = 0:2, labels = m5_labels(sensory_label)),
      age_start = baseline_age + start
    )

  # ---- 3) Checks -----------------------------------------------------------
  stopifnot(
    !anyNA(df_tv$frail_hist_start),            # every opening wave found
    !anyNA(df_tv$ctx_lag),                     # tv_cc is complete on these
    all(df_tv$stop > df_tv$start),
    # current frailty at start implies frailty history at start
    all(df_tv$frail_hist_start[df_tv$frail_start == 1] == 1),
    # at most one event per person, and nothing after it
    all(tapply(df_tv$dementia_event, df_tv$idauniq, sum) <= 1)
  )

  df_tv
}

# ==========================================================================
# Fit Model 5
# ==========================================================================
fit_m5 <- function(dat, label) {
  fit <- coxph(
    Surv(start, stop, dementia_event) ~
      ctx_lag + baseline_age +
      Gender + Race + Education + Marital_status +
      emp_lag + smoke_lag + alcohol_lag,
    data = dat, cluster = idauniq, ties = "efron", na.action = na.omit
  )

  # counts from the rows the model actually used
  used <- if (is.null(fit$na.action)) dat else dat[-fit$na.action, ]

  cat("\n============================================================\n")
  cat(label, "Model 5 (3-level, reference = no sensory impairment)\n")
  cat("============================================================\n")
  cat("Fitted sample - intervals:", fit$n,
      "| persons:", dplyr::n_distinct(used$idauniq),
      "| events:", fit$nevent, "\n")
  if (!is.null(fit$na.action))
    cat("  (", length(fit$na.action), "intervals dropped for missing covariates )\n")

  cat("\n--- Cox fit ---\n")
  print(summary(fit))

  zph <- cox.zph(fit)
  cat("\n--- PH check (Schoenfeld residuals) ---\n")
  print(zph)

  attr(fit, "zph")  <- zph
  attr(fit, "used") <- used
  fit
}

# ==========================================================================
# Category table: intervals, person-years, persons, events, rate, age, HR
# ==========================================================================
m5_category_table <- function(fit, label) {
  used <- attr(fit, "used")
  ci   <- summary(fit)$conf.int
  hr_row <- function(lvl) {
    nm <- paste0("ctx_lag", lvl)
    if (!nm %in% rownames(ci)) return("1 (ref)")
    sprintf("%.2f (%.2f-%.2f)", ci[nm, 1], ci[nm, 3], ci[nm, 4])
  }

  tab <- used %>%
    group_by(ctx_lag) %>%
    summarise(
      intervals    = n(),
      person_years = sum(stop - start),
      persons      = n_distinct(idauniq),
      events       = sum(dementia_event),
      mean_age     = mean(age_start),
      sd_age       = sd(age_start),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      category     = m5_display[as.integer(ctx_lag)],
      pct_pyrs     = 100 * person_years / sum(person_years),
      rate_1000py  = 1000 * events / person_years,
      HR_95CI      = vapply(as.character(ctx_lag), hr_row, character(1))
    ) %>%
    dplyr::select(category, intervals, person_years, pct_pyrs, persons,
                  events, rate_1000py, mean_age, sd_age, HR_95CI)

  cat("\n[", label, "] Model 5 categories (fitted sample)\n", sep = "")
  cat("  persons: people contributing any interval to the category;",
      "a person can contribute to more than one category,",
      "so persons do not add up to the total.\n")
  print(as.data.frame(tab), digits = 3, row.names = FALSE)
  invisible(tab)
}

# ==========================================================================
# Within-exposed contrast: category 2 vs category 1
#   A direct comparison of the two sensory contexts (frailty recorded vs not)
#   among people with sensory impairment. It is not an interaction test:
#   effect modification by frailty is tested in Model 4 (Supplementary Table 34).
# ==========================================================================
contrast_frailty_vs_no_frailty <- function(fit, label) {
  co <- coef(fit)
  vc <- vcov(fit)                      # robust (cluster) covariance
  i_no_fr  <- grep("no frailty yet",  names(co), fixed = TRUE)
  i_fr_yes <- grep("frailty present", names(co), fixed = TRUE)
  stopifnot(length(i_no_fr) == 1, length(i_fr_yes) == 1)

  z975 <- qnorm(0.975)
  L <- numeric(length(co))
  L[i_fr_yes] <-  1
  L[i_no_fr]  <- -1

  est <- sum(L * co)
  se  <- sqrt(drop(t(L) %*% vc %*% L))
  z   <- est / se
  p   <- 2 * pnorm(-abs(z))
  ci  <- exp(est + c(-1, 1) * z975 * se)

  lvl_hr <- function(i) exp(co[i] + c(0, -1, 1) * z975 * sqrt(vc[i, i]))
  hr1 <- lvl_hr(i_no_fr)
  hr2 <- lvl_hr(i_fr_yes)

  cat(sprintf("\n[%s] Category HRs vs no sensory impairment:\n", label))
  cat(sprintf("  Before frailty onset        : %.2f (%.2f-%.2f)\n", hr1[1], hr1[2], hr1[3]))
  cat(sprintf("  With or after frailty onset : %.2f (%.2f-%.2f)\n", hr2[1], hr2[2], hr2[3]))
  cat(sprintf("  Ratio (with or after / before) = %.2f (95%% CI %.2f-%.2f), z = %.2f, p = %.4f\n",
              exp(est), ci[1], ci[2], z, p))

  invisible(list(estimate = est, se = se, z = z, p = p,
                 ratio = exp(est), ci = ci,
                 hr_before = hr1, hr_with_after = hr2))
}

# ==========================================================================
# Make-up of category 2 by observed order of first onsets (Supplementary
#   Table 42). Uses only onsets at or before each interval's start.
# ==========================================================================
m5_category2_makeup <- function(fit, label) {
  used <- attr(fit, "used")

  tab <- used %>%
    filter(as.integer(ctx_lag) == 3L) %>%
    mutate(
      sequence = case_when(
        first_sensory_time == 0 & first_frail_time == 0 ~
          "Both present at baseline (order unknown)",
        first_sensory_time == first_frail_time ~
          "Both first observed at the same wave",
        first_sensory_time <  first_frail_time ~
          "Sensory impairment observed first",
        first_sensory_time >  first_frail_time ~
          "Frailty observed first"
      ),
      sequence = factor(sequence, levels = c(
        "Both present at baseline (order unknown)",
        "Both first observed at the same wave",
        "Sensory impairment observed first",
        "Frailty observed first"))
    )
  stopifnot(!anyNA(tab$sequence))

  out <- tab %>%
    group_by(sequence, .drop = FALSE) %>%
    summarise(
      intervals    = n(),
      person_years = sum(stop - start),
      persons      = n_distinct(idauniq),
      events       = sum(dementia_event),
      currently_frail_pct = 100 * mean(frail_start == 1),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    mutate(pct_pyrs = 100 * person_years / sum(person_years))

  cat("\n[", label, "] Make-up of 'with or after frailty onset' person-time\n", sep = "")
  cat("  currently_frail_pct: share of intervals still frail at their start",
      "(the rest had recovered below FI 0.25 but keep their frailty history)\n")
  print(as.data.frame(out), digits = 3, row.names = FALSE)
  invisible(out)
}

# ==========================================================================
# Movement between categories from one interval to the next
# ==========================================================================
m5_transitions <- function(fit, label) {
  used <- attr(fit, "used") %>%
    arrange(idauniq, start) %>%
    group_by(idauniq) %>%
    mutate(from = lag(as.integer(ctx_lag)),
           to   = as.integer(ctx_lag)) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    filter(!is.na(from))

  tr <- table(from = factor(m5_display[used$from], levels = m5_display),
              to   = factor(m5_display[used$to],   levels = m5_display))

  cat("\n[", label, "] Category at consecutive intervals (counts; rows = earlier)\n", sep = "")
  print(tr)
  cat("\n  Row percentages:\n")
  print(round(100 * prop.table(tr, 1), 1))
  cat("\n  Sensory impairment reported as resolved (category 1 or 2 -> reference):",
      sum(tr[2:3, 1]), "of", sum(tr[2:3, ]), "transitions from categories 1-2\n")
  invisible(tr)
}

# ==========================================================================
# One example timeline
#   Picks the first person whose intervals run through categories 0, 1, 2,
#   to illustrate how intervals are classified. The ID is replaced.
# ==========================================================================
m5_example_timeline <- function(fit, label) {
  used <- attr(fit, "used")
  ids <- used %>%
    arrange(idauniq, start) %>%
    group_by(idauniq) %>%
    summarise(seq = paste(as.integer(ctx_lag) - 1L, collapse = ""),
              .groups = "drop") %>%
    filter(grepl("^0+1+2+$", seq)) %>%
    pull(idauniq)
  if (!length(ids)) { cat("\n[", label, "] no 0 -> 1 -> 2 example found\n"); return(invisible(NULL)) }

  ex <- used %>%
    filter(idauniq == ids[1]) %>%
    arrange(start) %>%
    transmute(
      interval_years = sprintf("(%g, %g]", start, stop),
      sensory_at_start = sensory_start,
      frail_at_start   = frail_start,
      frailty_recorded_by_start = frail_hist_start,
      category = m5_display[as.integer(ctx_lag)],
      dementia_event
    )

  cat("\n[", label, "] Example participant (", length(ids),
      " people follow a 0 -> 1 -> 2 path)\n", sep = "")
  print(as.data.frame(ex), row.names = FALSE)
  invisible(ex)
}

# ==========================================================================
# Person-level description of the observed order of first onsets
#   DESCRIPTIVE ONLY: uses each person's whole follow-up, so it is not, and
#   must not be, used to classify intervals. Restricted to the people and
#   waves of the Model 5 sample (assessed waves up to 2018, up to the first
#   dementia wave).
# ==========================================================================
build_person_level <- function(dat, sensory_var, sensory_label,
                               panel_df = panel_df_eligible) {
  ids <- unique(dat$idauniq)

  panel_df %>%
    mutate(
      idauniq        = as.character(idauniq),
      year          = as.integer(year),
      baseline_year = as.integer(baseline_year),
      time          = as.numeric(year - baseline_year),
      .sensory      = .data[[sensory_var]]
    ) %>%
    filter(idauniq %in% ids, !is.na(dementia), year <= last_wave) %>%
    group_by(idauniq) %>%
    filter(time <= suppressWarnings(min(c(time[dementia == 1], Inf)))) %>%
    summarise(
      sensory_onset_time = if (any(.sensory == 1, na.rm = TRUE))
                             min(time[.sensory == 1], na.rm = TRUE)
                           else NA_real_,
      frailty_onset_time = if (any(frailty == 1, na.rm = TRUE))
                             min(time[frailty == 1], na.rm = TRUE)
                           else NA_real_,
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      sequence = case_when(
        is.na(sensory_onset_time) ~
          paste0("No ", sensory_label, " observed"),
        is.na(frailty_onset_time) ~
          paste0(sensory_label, ", never frail during follow-up"),
        sensory_onset_time == 0 & frailty_onset_time == 0 ~
          "Both present at baseline",
        sensory_onset_time < frailty_onset_time ~
          paste0(sensory_label, " observed before frailty"),
        sensory_onset_time == frailty_onset_time ~
          "Both first observed at the same wave",
        sensory_onset_time > frailty_onset_time ~
          paste0(sensory_label, " observed after frailty")
      )
    )
}

# ==========================================================================
# 1) Build datasets (same rows as Models 1-4)
# ==========================================================================
stopifnot(exists("tv_cc"))

df_tv_hearing <- build_m5_dataset(
  sensory_var   = "hearing_loss",
  sensory_lag   = "hearing_lag",
  sensory_label = "Hearing loss"
)

df_tv_vision <- build_m5_dataset(
  sensory_var   = "vision_overall",
  sensory_lag   = "vision_lag",
  sensory_label = "Vision loss"
)

# ==========================================================================
# 2) Fit Model 5
# ==========================================================================
fit_m5_hearing <- fit_m5(df_tv_hearing, "HEARING")
fit_m5_vision  <- fit_m5(df_tv_vision,  "VISION")

# Event reconciliation: Model 5 should use the same events as Model 4
cat("\nEvents - Model 4 sample:", sum(tv_cc$event),
    "| Model 5 hearing:", fit_m5_hearing$nevent,
    "| Model 5 vision:",  fit_m5_vision$nevent, "\n")

# ==========================================================================
# 3) Category tables and within-exposed contrast
# ==========================================================================
m5_tab_hearing <- m5_category_table(fit_m5_hearing, "HEARING")
m5_tab_vision  <- m5_category_table(fit_m5_vision,  "VISION")

m5_con_hearing <- contrast_frailty_vs_no_frailty(fit_m5_hearing, "HEARING")
m5_con_vision  <- contrast_frailty_vs_no_frailty(fit_m5_vision,  "VISION")

# ==========================================================================
# 4) Descriptives of the Model 5 categories
# ==========================================================================
m5_mix_hearing <- m5_category2_makeup(fit_m5_hearing, "HEARING")
m5_mix_vision  <- m5_category2_makeup(fit_m5_vision,  "VISION")

m5_tr_hearing  <- m5_transitions(fit_m5_hearing, "HEARING")
m5_tr_vision   <- m5_transitions(fit_m5_vision,  "VISION")

m5_example_timeline(fit_m5_hearing, "HEARING")

# ==========================================================================
# 5) Person-level description (not used in any model)
# ==========================================================================
person_hearing <- build_person_level(df_tv_hearing, "hearing_loss",   "Hearing loss")
person_vision  <- build_person_level(df_tv_vision,  "vision_overall", "Vision loss")

cat("\nObserved order of first onsets, whole follow-up (descriptive) - HEARING:\n")
print(table(person_hearing$sequence, useNA = "ifany"))
cat("\nObserved order of first onsets, whole follow-up (descriptive) - VISION:\n")
print(table(person_vision$sequence, useNA = "ifany"))

m5_category_table(fit_m5_hearing, "HEARING"); m5_category_table(fit_m5_vision, "VISION")
m5_category2_makeup(fit_m5_hearing, "HEARING"); m5_category2_makeup(fit_m5_vision, "VISION")
m5_example_timeline(fit_m5_hearing, "HEARING")
```

# PAF — Hearing Loss, Vision Loss, Frailty (ELSA)
```{r}
# PAF for Models 1-5 (ELSA, dementia outcome)
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Models 1-4 use tv_cc (counting-process: tstart/tstop, *_lag exposures).
# Model 5 uses df_tv_hearing / df_tv_vision (start/stop, ctx_lag factor).
# Prevalence = person-time-weighted within each fit's analytic dataset.
# person-time-weighted exposure prevalence p and the model hazard ratio,
#   PAF = p(HR - 1) / [1 + p(HR - 1)],
# and, for the three-level Model 5 exposure,
#   PAF_total = sum_k p_k(HR_k - 1) / [1 + sum_k p_k(HR_k - 1)],
#   PAF_k     = p_k(HR_k - 1)       / [1 + sum_j p_j(HR_j - 1)].
# 95% CIs: 10,000 Monte Carlo draws of the log-HR(s) from their robust
# (cluster) sampling distribution; p is treated as fixed.

PAF_SEED <- 20260509
PAF_NSIM <- 10000
z975     <- qnorm(0.975)

print_df <- function(x, digits = 4) {
  cat(capture.output(print(as.data.frame(x), row.names = FALSE,
                           digits = digits)), sep = "\n")
}

# ---- Formulas ---------------------------------------------------------------
paf_binary_fn <- function(p, HR) (p * (HR - 1)) / (p * (HR - 1) + 1)   # Levin

# ---- Prevalences --------------------------------------------------------------
# Person-time-weighted prevalence (binary 0/1 indicator)
prev_pt_binary <- function(dat, var, ts, tp) {
  pt <- dat[[tp]] - dat[[ts]]
  x  <- dat[[var]]
  sum(pt[x == 1], na.rm = TRUE) / sum(pt, na.rm = TRUE)
}

# Person-time-weighted prevalence per factor level
prev_pt_factor <- function(dat, var, ts, tp) {
  pt    <- dat[[tp]] - dat[[ts]]
  x     <- dat[[var]]
  total <- sum(pt, na.rm = TRUE)
  tibble(
    level = levels(x),
    p     = vapply(levels(x),
                   function(lv) sum(pt[x == lv], na.rm = TRUE) / total,
                   numeric(1))
  )
}

# Rows a fit actually used (Model 5 fits carry them; Models 1-4 use tv_cc)
fit_rows <- function(fit, dat) {
  used <- attr(fit, "used")
  if (!is.null(used)) return(used)
  if (!is.null(fit$na.action)) dat <- dat[-fit$na.action, ]
  stopifnot(nrow(dat) == fit$n)
  dat
}

# ---- Monte Carlo CIs ---------------------------------------------------------
paf_ci_binary <- function(fit, term, p, nsim = PAF_NSIM, seed = PAF_SEED) {
  b <- unname(coef(fit)[term])
  V <- vcov(fit)[term, term]                 # robust (cluster) variance
  stopifnot(!is.na(b), V > 0)
  set.seed(seed)
  sims <- rnorm(nsim, mean = b, sd = sqrt(V))
  pafs <- paf_binary_fn(p, exp(sims))
  tibble(
    HR     = exp(b),
    HR_lcl = exp(b - z975 * sqrt(V)),
    HR_ucl = exp(b + z975 * sqrt(V)),
    PAF = paf_binary_fn(p, exp(b)),
    lcl = unname(quantile(pafs, 0.025, na.rm = TRUE)),
    ucl = unname(quantile(pafs, 0.975, na.rm = TRUE))
  )
}

paf_ci_multicat <- function(fit, terms, p_vec, labels, nsim = PAF_NSIM,
                            seed = PAF_SEED) {
  b <- unname(coef(fit)[terms])
  V <- vcov(fit)[terms, terms, drop = FALSE]
  set.seed(seed)
  sims <- MASS::mvrnorm(nsim, mu = b, Sigma = V)
  if (is.vector(sims)) sims <- matrix(sims, ncol = length(terms))
  HRs <- exp(sims)

  # Levin, partitioned so that components add up to the total
  comp_mat      <- sweep(HRs - 1, 2, p_vec, `*`)
  s_all         <- rowSums(comp_mat)
  paf_total_sim <- s_all / (1 + s_all)
  paf_comp_sim  <- comp_mat / (1 + s_all)

  HR_est    <- exp(b)
  se        <- sqrt(diag(V))
  comp_est  <- p_vec * (HR_est - 1)
  s_all_est <- sum(comp_est)
  q <- function(x, pr) unname(quantile(x, pr, na.rm = TRUE))

  tibble(
    component = c("Total", labels),
    HR        = c(NA_real_, HR_est),
    HR_lcl    = c(NA_real_, exp(b - z975 * se)),
    HR_ucl    = c(NA_real_, exp(b + z975 * se)),
    PAF       = c(s_all_est / (1 + s_all_est), comp_est / (1 + s_all_est)),
    lcl       = c(q(paf_total_sim, 0.025), apply(paf_comp_sim, 2, q, 0.025)),
    ucl       = c(q(paf_total_sim, 0.975), apply(paf_comp_sim, 2, q, 0.975))
  )
}

# ============================================================================
# A) Prevalences in tv_cc (Models 1-4; every fit uses all tv_cc rows)
# ============================================================================
for (f in list(fit_m1_hearing, fit_m2_vision, fit_m3_frailty, fit_m4_frailty))
  stopifnot(f$n == nrow(tv_cc))

p_hearing_14 <- prev_pt_binary(tv_cc, "hearing_lag", "tstart", "tstop")
p_vision_14  <- prev_pt_binary(tv_cc, "vision_lag",  "tstart", "tstop")
p_frailty_14 <- prev_pt_binary(tv_cc, "frailty_lag", "tstart", "tstop")

cat("Person-time-weighted prevalence (tv_cc):\n")
cat(sprintf("  Hearing loss : %.4f\n", p_hearing_14))
cat(sprintf("  Vision loss  : %.4f\n", p_vision_14))
cat(sprintf("  Frailty      : %.4f\n", p_frailty_14))

# ============================================================================
# B) PAF for Models 1-4 (each exposure paired with its own model fit)
# ============================================================================
paf_row <- function(fit, term, p, model_label, exposure_label) {
  res <- paf_ci_binary(fit, term, p)
  tibble(model = model_label, exposure = exposure_label, p_pt = p) %>%
    bind_cols(res %>% rename(PAF_lcl = lcl, PAF_ucl = ucl))
}

paf_models_1_4 <- bind_rows(
  # Model 1 (unadjusted)
  paf_row(fit_m1_hearing, "hearing_lag", p_hearing_14, "M1 (unadjusted)", "Hearing loss"),
  paf_row(fit_m1_vision,  "vision_lag",  p_vision_14,  "M1 (unadjusted)", "Vision loss"),
  paf_row(fit_m1_frailty, "frailty_lag", p_frailty_14, "M1 (unadjusted)", "Frailty"),

  # Model 2 (+ age)
  paf_row(fit_m2_hearing, "hearing_lag", p_hearing_14, "M2 (+ age)", "Hearing loss"),
  paf_row(fit_m2_vision,  "vision_lag",  p_vision_14,  "M2 (+ age)", "Vision loss"),
  paf_row(fit_m2_frailty, "frailty_lag", p_frailty_14, "M2 (+ age)", "Frailty"),

  # Model 3 (+ sex, race, education, marital status, employment, smoking, alcohol)
  paf_row(fit_m3_hearing, "hearing_lag", p_hearing_14, "M3 (+ sociodemographic + lifestyle)", "Hearing loss"),
  paf_row(fit_m3_vision,  "vision_lag",  p_vision_14,  "M3 (+ sociodemographic + lifestyle)", "Vision loss"),
  paf_row(fit_m3_frailty, "frailty_lag", p_frailty_14, "M3 (+ sociodemographic + lifestyle)", "Frailty"),

  # Model 4 (primary): hearing/vision adjusted for frailty;
  # frailty from the mutually adjusted Cox
  paf_row(fit_m4_hearing, "hearing_lag", p_hearing_14, "M4 (hybrid, frailty-adj)", "Hearing loss"),
  paf_row(fit_m4_vision,  "vision_lag",  p_vision_14,  "M4 (hybrid, frailty-adj)", "Vision loss"),
  paf_row(fit_m4_frailty, "frailty_lag", p_frailty_14, "M4 (mutually adjusted)",   "Frailty")
)

# ============================================================================
# C) PAF for Model 5 (3-level ctx_lag, hearing and vision separately)
#    Component PAFs for each non-reference level + total PAF.
#    Model 5 is not adjusted for frailty, so its total is not comparable
#    with the Model 4 PAF; the level-1 component is negative when HR < 1.
# ============================================================================
paf_model5 <- function(fit, dat, model_label) {
  dat <- fit_rows(fit, dat)
  stopifnot(is.factor(dat$ctx_lag))
  exposed_lvls <- levels(dat$ctx_lag)[-1]

  prev_tab  <- prev_pt_factor(dat, "ctx_lag", "start", "stop")
  p_exposed <- setNames(prev_tab$p[match(exposed_lvls, prev_tab$level)],
                        exposed_lvls)
  stopifnot(all(!is.na(p_exposed)), all(p_exposed > 0))

  terms <- paste0("ctx_lag", exposed_lvls)
  miss  <- setdiff(terms, names(coef(fit)))
  if (length(miss))
    stop("Missing coefficients in Model 5 fit: ", paste(miss, collapse = ", "))

  tab <- paf_ci_multicat(fit, terms, p_exposed, exposed_lvls)
  stopifnot(abs(sum(tab$PAF[-1]) - tab$PAF[1]) < 1e-10)   # components add up

  tab %>%
    mutate(model  = model_label,
           exposure = component,
           p_pt   = c(sum(p_exposed), unname(p_exposed))) %>%
    dplyr::select(model, exposure, p_pt, HR, HR_lcl, HR_ucl,
                  PAF, PAF_lcl = lcl, PAF_ucl = ucl)
}

paf_m5_hearing <- paf_model5(fit_m5_hearing, df_tv_hearing, "M5 (hearing context)")
paf_m5_vision  <- paf_model5(fit_m5_vision,  df_tv_vision,  "M5 (vision context)")

# ============================================================================
# D) Combined summary
# ============================================================================
fmt_pct <- function(est, lo, hi)
  sprintf("%.1f (%.1f to %.1f)", 100 * est, 100 * lo, 100 * hi)
fmt_hr  <- function(est, lo, hi)
  ifelse(is.na(est), "", sprintf("%.2f (%.2f-%.2f)", est, lo, hi))

paf_all <- bind_rows(paf_models_1_4, paf_m5_hearing, paf_m5_vision) %>%
  mutate(
    HR_CI  = fmt_hr(HR, HR_lcl, HR_ucl),
    PAF_CI = fmt_pct(PAF, PAF_lcl, PAF_ucl)
  )

cat("\n=== PAF (Levin formula) - Models 1-5 ===\n")
print_df(paf_all %>% dplyr::select(model, exposure, p_pt, HR_CI, PAF_CI))


```


# Parametric g-formula PAF (ELSA), Models 1-4: sensitivity analysis for the
# Levin PAFs
```{r}
# Run after the Models 1-4 chunk. Uses tv_cc, panel_df_eligible and
# baseline_df_eligible.
#
# Same set-up as Cox Models 1-4; only the PAF method differs:
#   - participants: exactly those in tv_cc;
#   - dementia events and follow-up end: taken from tv_cc itself, so the
#     events and each person's last interval are the Cox ones;
#   - covariates: only from waves with an assessed dementia status up to
#     2018 (the waves in df0), held from the wave that opens an interval,
#     as hearing_lag, vision_lag, frailty_lag, emp_lag, smoke_lag and
#     alcohol_lag are;
#   - time-fixed covariates: baseline_age, Gender, Race, Education,
#     Marital_status from baseline_df_eligible, as in baseline_invariant;
#   - censoring: follow-up ends at the last tv_cc interval; loss to
#     follow-up (including unrecorded deaths: ELSA has no usable mortality
#     data) and the end of the study are censoring, exactly as in the Cox
#     models;
#   - the dementia model is fitted on the tv_cc person-time only, with the
#     same terms as each Cox formula;
#   - time scale: years since baseline (k = biennial interval), with a
#     separate baseline risk for each interval (factor(k)), the discrete
#     counterpart of the Cox baseline hazard.
# The one structural addition: the g-formula simulates covariate
# histories, so it needs an unbroken history per person. Where a Cox
# interval was dropped because a lagged covariate was missing, that
# interval is kept only as covariate history (value carried forward); it
# is not used in the dementia model. Counts are printed by build_gf_data.
#
# Estimand. For the intervention g = "eliminate the exposure (hearing
# impairment, vision impairment or frailty) at every wave",
#   PAF_g = [Risk(natural course) - Risk(under g)] / Risk(natural course),
# where Risk is the cumulative risk of dementia by a fixed horizon
# (default 8 biennial intervals = 16 years) under the same censoring
# assumption as the Cox models. This is a risk-based PAF, not a
# hazard-ratio-based one, so the numbers are not expected to equal the
# Levin PAFs exactly.
#
# Method (parametric g-formula; Robins 1986; Taubman et al. 2009;
# McGrath et al., Patterns 2020, which describes the gfoRmula package):
#   1. Person-wave data on the biennial grid. Waves without an assessment
#      are filled forward (last observation carried forward), so a Cox
#      interval spanning a missed wave becomes two 2-year intervals with
#      the same covariates and the event (if any) in the second.
#   2. Pooled logistic models, fitted on the observed data, for each
#      time-varying covariate given its past (wave k-1) and the covariates
#      simulated before it at wave k; and for dementia by the next wave
#      (the discrete-time version of the Cox model). Covariates at the
#      start of an interval predict the outcome over it (one-wave lag).
#   3. Monte Carlo simulation of every participant's covariate history
#      from the observed baseline, under no intervention (natural course)
#      and with the exposure eliminated; risks are accumulated from the
#      predicted dementia hazards.
#   4. Non-parametric bootstrap over participants for 95% CIs.
#
# Mapping to the Cox models (adjustment set = variables in the g-formula):
# (the dementia model uses the same terms as the Cox formula)
#   M1  hearing_lag | vision_lag | frailty_lag
#   M2  + baseline_age
#   M3  + Gender, Race, Education, Marital_status,
#        emp_lag, smoke_lag, alcohol_lag
#   M4  hearing:  M3 + frailty_lag          (fit_m4_hearing)
#       vision:   M3 + frailty_lag          (fit_m4_vision)
#       frailty:  M3 + hearing_lag + vision_lag (fit_m4_frailty)
#        In the g-formula the time-varying covariates are also simulated
#        over time. Frailty is simulated and can respond to earlier
#        sensory impairment, so the M4 g-formula PAF is a TOTAL effect,
#        including any pathway through frailty (Cox Model 4 instead
#        conditions on frailty).
# Model 5 is not included: its exposure is a joint sensory x frailty-history
# category, and "removing" a category has no single well-defined
# intervention (frailty history cannot be undone, and the categories are
# themselves changed by the intervention). Its PAFs stay with Levin.
# ==========================================================================

suppressPackageStartupMessages({ library(dplyr); library(tidyr) })

GF <- list(
  year_end = last_wave,      # last wave with dementia ascertainment
  K        = 8L,         # intervals simulated (8 x 2 years = 16 years)
  report_k = c(5L, 8L),  # report risk at 10 and 16 years. Baselines are
                         # 2002-2008, so every cohort is followed for 10
                         # years; 16 years rests on the 2002 cohort only
  B        = 200L,       # bootstrap replicates (0 = point estimates only;
                         # run once with B = 0 and time it: 12 models x
                         # (B + 1) fits, so the bootstrap can take hours)
  seed     = 20260509,
  # Parallel workers for the bootstrap. Each worker is a full copy of R
  # (about 1 GB here), so more workers need more memory; 4 is safe on a
  # 16 GB machine. Use 1 to run in the main session only.
  cores    = min(4L, max(1L, parallel::detectCores() - 1L)),
  # Each model's result is saved here when it finishes, so an interrupted
  # run resumes where it stopped.
  cache_dir = file.path(results_dir, "gf_cache_ELSA")
)

gf_print <- function(x, digits = 4)
  cat(capture.output(print(as.data.frame(x), row.names = FALSE,
                           digits = digits)), sep = "\n")

to01 <- function(x) {
  x <- suppressWarnings(as.integer(as.character(x)))
  stopifnot(all(x %in% c(0L, 1L, NA)))
  x
}

TV_ALL <- c("emp", "smoke", "alcohol", "frail", "hearing", "vision")

# ==========================================================================
# 1) Person-wave data
# ==========================================================================
build_gf_data <- function(panel_df    = panel_df_eligible,
                          baseline_df = baseline_df_eligible,
                          cox_df      = tv_cc,
                          year_end    = GF$year_end) {

  ids <- unique(as.character(cox_df$idauniq))

  # Time-fixed covariates, as baseline_invariant in the Cox chunk
  base <- baseline_df %>%
    mutate(idauniq = as.character(idauniq)) %>%
    filter(idauniq %in% ids) %>%
    distinct(idauniq, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
    transmute(
      idauniq,
      baseline_age   = as.numeric(age),
      Gender         = factor(Gender),
      Race           = factor(Race),
      Education      = factor(Education),
      Marital_status = factor(Marital_status)
    )

  # Follow-up end and dementia event, taken from the Cox sample itself
  cox_ends <- cox_df %>%
    mutate(idauniq = as.character(idauniq)) %>%
    group_by(idauniq) %>%
    summarise(last_k = as.integer(round(max(tstop) / 2)),
              dem_k  = if (any(event == 1L))
                         as.integer(round(max(tstop[event == 1L]) / 2)) else NA_integer_,
              .groups = "drop")
  stopifnot(all(is.na(cox_ends$dem_k) | cox_ends$dem_k == cox_ends$last_k))

  # Covariates from the assessed waves the Cox models use (df0)
  pan <- panel_df %>%
    mutate(idauniq = as.character(idauniq),
           year = as.integer(year), baseline_year = as.integer(baseline_year)) %>%
    filter(idauniq %in% ids, !is.na(dementia), year <= year_end)
  off_grid <- sum((pan$year - pan$baseline_year) %% 2 != 0)
  pan <- pan %>%
    filter((year - baseline_year) %% 2 == 0) %>%
    transmute(idauniq, baseline_year, k = as.integer((year - baseline_year) / 2),
              hearing = to01(hearing_loss), vision = to01(vision_overall),
              frail = to01(frailty), emp = to01(Employment),
              smoke = to01(Smoking), alcohol = to01(Alcohol))

  ends <- cox_ends %>%
    left_join(pan %>% distinct(idauniq, baseline_year), by = "idauniq")
  stopifnot(!anyNA(ends$baseline_year))

  # Grid: intervals k = 0..last_k - 1 (interval k runs from wave k to k + 1)
  dat <- ends %>%
    tidyr::uncount(last_k, .id = "k1") %>%
    mutate(k = k1 - 1L) %>% dplyr::select(-k1) %>%
    left_join(pan %>% dplyr::select(-baseline_year), by = c("idauniq", "k")) %>%
    arrange(idauniq, k)

  # Which grid intervals are Cox person-time
  cox_k <- cox_df %>%
    mutate(idauniq = as.character(idauniq),
           k0 = as.integer(round(tstart / 2)), k1 = as.integer(round(tstop / 2))) %>%
    tidyr::uncount(k1 - k0, .id = "j") %>%
    transmute(idauniq, k = k0 + j - 1L, in_cox = 1L)
  dat <- dat %>% left_join(cox_k, by = c("idauniq", "k")) %>%
    mutate(in_cox = coalesce(in_cox, 0L))

  # cov_obs = 1: all covariates observed at this wave (used to fit the
  # covariate models); otherwise carried forward, or back from the first
  # observed wave if missing at baseline
  dat$cov_obs <- as.integer(complete.cases(dat[, TV_ALL]))
  n_back <- sum(is.na(dat[dat$k == 0L, TV_ALL]))
  dat <- dat %>%
    group_by(idauniq) %>%
    tidyr::fill(all_of(TV_ALL), .direction = "downup") %>%
    mutate(
      frail_hist = cummax(frail),
      Y = as.integer(!is.na(dem_k) & k + 1L == dem_k)
    ) %>%
    mutate(across(c(all_of(TV_ALL), frail_hist), dplyr::lag, .names = "lag1_{.col}")) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    left_join(base, by = "idauniq") %>%
    dplyr::select(idauniq, k, Y, in_cox, cov_obs, all_of(TV_ALL), frail_hist,
                  starts_with("lag1_"), baseline_age, Gender, Race,
                  Education, Marital_status)

  n_cox_iv <- sum(dat$in_cox == 1L)
  stopifnot(!anyNA(dat[, c("Y", TV_ALL, "baseline_age", "Gender", "Race",
                           "Education", "Marital_status")]),
            all(tapply(dat$Y, dat$idauniq, sum) <= 1),
            n_distinct(dat$idauniq) == length(ids),
            sum(dat$Y[dat$in_cox == 1L]) == sum(cox_df$event),
            sum(dat$Y) == sum(cox_df$event),
            isTRUE(all.equal(2 * n_cox_iv, sum(cox_df$tstop - cox_df$tstart))))

  cat("g-formula data (same participants, events and person-time as Cox Models 1-4):\n")
  cat("  participants:", n_distinct(dat$idauniq), "(tv_cc:", length(ids), ")",
      "| dementia events:", sum(dat$Y), "(tv_cc:", sum(cox_df$event), ")\n")
  cat("  person-years in the dementia model:", round(2 * n_cox_iv),
      "(tv_cc:", round(sum(cox_df$tstop - cox_df$tstart)), ")\n")
  cat("  2-year intervals:", n_cox_iv, "used in the dementia model +",
      sum(dat$in_cox == 0L),
      "kept only as covariate history (Cox interval dropped for a missing covariate)\n")
  cat("  covariate values carried forward:", sum(dat$cov_obs == 0L & dat$k > 0L),
      "rows | back-filled at baseline:", n_back, "values | off-grid waves dropped:",
      off_grid, "\n")
  at_risk <- table(factor(dat$k[dat$in_cox == 1L], levels = 0:max(dat$k)))
  cat("  at risk by interval k:", paste0(names(at_risk), "=", at_risk, collapse = " "), "\n")
  if (GF$K > max(dat$k) + 1L || at_risk[GF$K] < 1000)
    warning("Few or no participants are observed in interval k = ", GF$K - 1L,
            "; consider a smaller GF$K and GF$report_k.")
  dat
}

# Observed cumulative risk, 1 - Kaplan-Meier, on the Cox person-time
# (censoring as in the Cox models), for the natural-course check
observed_risk <- function(dat, K = GF$K) {
  at <- dat %>% filter(in_cox == 1L) %>%
    group_by(k) %>% summarise(n = n(), y = sum(Y), .groups = "drop")
  h <- at$y[match(0:(K - 1), at$k)] / at$n[match(0:(K - 1), at$k)]
  1 - cumprod(1 - h)
}

# ==========================================================================
# 2) Model specifications (one per Cox model and exposure)
# ==========================================================================
B3 <- c("baseline_age", "Gender", "Race", "Education", "Marital_status")
L3 <- c("emp", "smoke", "alcohol")

mk_spec <- function(model, exposure, tv, base = character(0))
  list(model = model, exposure = exposure, tv = tv, base = base)

gf_specs <- list(
  M1_hearing = mk_spec("M1", "hearing", "hearing"),
  M2_hearing = mk_spec("M2", "hearing", "hearing", "baseline_age"),
  M3_hearing = mk_spec("M3", "hearing", c(L3, "hearing"), B3),
  M4_hearing = mk_spec("M4", "hearing", c(L3, "frail", "hearing"), B3),

  M1_vision  = mk_spec("M1", "vision", "vision"),
  M2_vision  = mk_spec("M2", "vision", "vision", "baseline_age"),
  M3_vision  = mk_spec("M3", "vision", c(L3, "vision"), B3),
  M4_vision  = mk_spec("M4", "vision", c(L3, "frail", "vision"), B3),

  M1_frailty = mk_spec("M1", "frail", "frail"),
  M2_frailty = mk_spec("M2", "frail", "frail", "baseline_age"),
  M3_frailty = mk_spec("M3", "frail", c(L3, "frail"), B3),
  M4_frailty = mk_spec("M4", "frail", c(L3, "frail", "hearing", "vision"), B3)
)

# Intervention (every spec): set the exposure to 0 at every wave, for
# everyone, from baseline onwards.

# ==========================================================================
# 3) Fit, simulate, estimate
# ==========================================================================
TIME_COV <- c("k", "I(k^2)")   # covariate models
TIME_OUT <- "factor(k)"        # dementia: one baseline risk per interval,
                               # like the Cox baseline hazard

# Logistic fit that keeps only what prediction needs (a full glm object
# stores copies of the data, which multiplies memory across workers)
lean_glm <- function(formula, data) {
  f <- glm(formula, family = binomial, data = data, model = FALSE, y = FALSE)
  b <- coef(f); b[is.na(b)] <- 0
  list(coef = b, terms = delete.response(terms(f)),
       xlev = f$xlevels, contrasts = f$contrasts)
}
pred_lean <- function(fit, newdata) {
  mf <- model.frame(fit$terms, newdata, xlev = fit$xlev)
  X  <- model.matrix(fit$terms, mf, contrasts.arg = fit$contrasts)
  plogis(drop(X %*% fit$coef[colnames(X)]))
}

fit_gf_models <- function(dat, spec) {
  tv <- spec$tv
  dk <- dat[dat$k >= 1 & dat$cov_obs == 1L, ]   # observed waves only
  cov_fits <- list()
  for (i in seq_along(tv)) {
    v   <- tv[i]
    rhs <- c(tv[seq_len(i - 1)], paste0("lag1_", tv),
             if (v == "frail") "lag1_frail_hist", spec$base, TIME_COV)
    cov_fits[[v]] <- lean_glm(reformulate(rhs, v), dk)
  }
  out_rhs <- c(tv, spec$base, TIME_OUT)
  list(cov = cov_fits,                          # dementia: tv_cc person-time only
       Y = lean_glm(reformulate(out_rhs, "Y"), dat[dat$in_cox == 1L, ]))
}

# int_var = NULL: natural course; otherwise the variable set to 0 at every wave
simulate_gf <- function(fits, spec, start, int_var = NULL, K = GF$K, seed = GF$seed) {
  set.seed(seed)                       # common random numbers: natural course vs intervention
  tv  <- spec$tv
  n   <- nrow(start)
  cur <- start
  prev_hist <- rep(0L, n)
  S <- rep(1, n); cum <- rep(0, n); cif <- numeric(K)

  for (k in 0:(K - 1)) {
    cur$k <- k
    if (k > 0) {
      for (v in tv) cur[[paste0("lag1_", v)]] <- prev[[v]]
      cur$lag1_frail_hist <- prev$frail_hist
    }
    for (v in tv) {
      if (k > 0) {
        p <- pred_lean(fits$cov[[v]], cur)
        cur[[v]] <- rbinom(n, 1L, p)
      }
      if (v == "frail") cur$frail_hist <- pmax(prev_hist, cur$frail)
      if (!is.null(int_var) && int_var == v) {
        cur[[v]][] <- 0L
        if (v == "frail") cur$frail_hist <- pmax(prev_hist, cur$frail)
      }
    }
    if ("frail" %in% tv) prev_hist <- cur$frail_hist
    h <- pred_lean(fits$Y, cur)
    cum <- cum + S * h
    S   <- S * (1 - h)
    cif[k + 1] <- mean(cum)
    prev <- cur
  }
  cif
}

est_gf <- function(spec, dat, seed = GF$seed) {
  fits  <- fit_gf_models(dat, spec)
  start <- dat[dat$k == 0L, ]
  if (!"frail_hist" %in% names(start)) start$frail_hist <- 0L
  nc    <- simulate_gf(fits, spec, start, NULL,          seed = seed)
  r     <- simulate_gf(fits, spec, start, spec$exposure, seed = seed)
  est   <- tibble(horizon_k = GF$report_k,
                  risk_nc   = nc[GF$report_k], risk_int = r[GF$report_k],
                  PAF       = (nc[GF$report_k] - r[GF$report_k]) / nc[GF$report_k])
  list(est = est, nc = nc)
}

boot_gf <- function(spec, dat, B = GF$B, cores = GF$cores) {
  if (B < 1) return(NULL)
  idx <- split(seq_len(nrow(dat)), dat$idauniq)
  one <- function(b) {
    set.seed(GF$seed + b)
    pick <- sample(names(idx), length(idx), replace = TRUE)
    rows <- unlist(idx[pick], use.names = FALSE)
    bd   <- dat[rows, ]
    bd$idauniq <- rep(seq_along(pick), lengths(idx[pick]))
    out <- tryCatch(est_gf(spec, bd, seed = GF$seed + b)$est,
                    error = function(e) NULL)
    if (!is.null(out)) out$b <- b
    rm(bd); invisible(gc(verbose = FALSE))
    out
  }
  if (cores <= 1) {
    res <- lapply(seq_len(B), one)
  } else if (.Platform$OS.type != "windows") {
    res <- parallel::mclapply(seq_len(B), one, mc.cores = cores)
  } else {                             # Windows: socket cluster
    cl <- parallel::makeCluster(cores)
    on.exit(parallel::stopCluster(cl), add = TRUE)
    parallel::clusterEvalQ(cl, suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(dplyr)))
    parallel::clusterExport(cl, c("GF", "TIME_COV", "TIME_OUT", "lean_glm", "pred_lean",
                                  "fit_gf_models", "simulate_gf", "est_gf"),
                            envir = globalenv())
    res <- parallel::parLapply(cl, seq_len(B), one)
  }
  bind_rows(res)
}

run_gf <- function(spec, dat, B = GF$B) {
  t0  <- Sys.time()
  pe  <- est_gf(spec, dat)
  bs  <- boot_gf(spec, dat, B)
  out <- pe$est %>% mutate(model = spec$model, exposure = spec$exposure, .before = 1)
  if (!is.null(bs) && nrow(bs)) {
    ci <- bs %>% group_by(horizon_k) %>%
      summarise(PAF_lcl = quantile(PAF, 0.025), PAF_ucl = quantile(PAF, 0.975),
                n_boot = n(), .groups = "drop")
    out <- out %>% left_join(ci, by = "horizon_k")
  } else out <- out %>% mutate(PAF_lcl = NA_real_, PAF_ucl = NA_real_, n_boot = 0L)
  cat(sprintf("  %-12s done in %.1f min\n", paste(spec$model, spec$exposure),
              as.numeric(difftime(Sys.time(), t0, units = "mins"))))
  list(table = out, nc = pe$nc)
}

# ==========================================================================
# 4) Run
# ==========================================================================
gf_dat <- build_gf_data()

# Quick timing check before committing to the bootstrap:
#   system.time(est_gf(gf_specs$M4_frailty, gf_dat))
dir.create(GF$cache_dir, showWarnings = FALSE)
gf_res <- setNames(lapply(names(gf_specs), function(nm) {
  f <- file.path(GF$cache_dir, sprintf("%s_B%d.rds", nm, GF$B))
  if (file.exists(f)) { cat("  ", nm, "loaded from", f, "\n"); return(readRDS(f)) }
  r <- run_gf(gf_specs[[nm]], gf_dat)
  saveRDS(r, f)
  r
}), names(gf_specs))

# ---- Natural-course check: simulated vs observed cumulative incidence ----
obs <- observed_risk(gf_dat)
nc_check <- bind_rows(lapply(names(gf_res), function(nm) tibble(
  spec = nm, horizon_k = GF$report_k,
  observed  = obs[GF$report_k],
  simulated = gf_res[[nm]]$nc[GF$report_k]))) %>%
  mutate(diff_pp = 100 * (simulated - observed))
cat("\n=== Natural course vs observed cumulative incidence of dementia ===\n")
cat("  (large differences point to misspecified models)\n")
gf_print(nc_check)

# ---- PAF table ----
gf_paf <- bind_rows(lapply(gf_res, `[[`, "table")) %>%
  mutate(
    years    = 2 * horizon_k,
    exposure = recode(exposure, hearing = "Hearing impairment",
                      vision = "Vision impairment", frail = "Frailty"),
    risk_nc  = sprintf("%.1f", 100 * risk_nc),
    risk_int = sprintf("%.1f", 100 * risk_int),
    PAF_CI   = ifelse(is.na(PAF_lcl), sprintf("%.1f", 100 * PAF),
                      sprintf("%.1f (%.1f to %.1f)", 100 * PAF,
                              100 * PAF_lcl, 100 * PAF_ucl))
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(model, exposure, years, risk_nc, risk_int, PAF_CI, n_boot)

cat("\n=== g-formula PAF (%), Models 1-4: cumulative risk of dementia ===\n")
cat("  risk_nc = natural course, risk_int = exposure eliminated at every wave (%)\n")
gf_print(gf_paf)
```

```{r}
library(survival)
library(survminer)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(scales)

KM_OUT_DIR <- output_dir   # figures; the data behind them go to results_dir

stopifnot(exists("tv_cc"), exists("baseline_df_eligible"))

to01 <- function(x) as.integer(as.character(x))

# ---- 0) One row per person: baseline status, follow-up end, event ----------
km_base <- tv_cc %>%
  mutate(idauniq = as.character(idauniq)) %>%
  group_by(idauniq) %>%
  summarise(t_event = max(tstop),               # last assessed wave <= 2018
            event   = as.integer(max(event)),   # follow-up stops at the event
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  left_join(baseline_df_eligible %>%
              mutate(idauniq = as.character(idauniq)) %>%
              distinct(idauniq, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
              transmute(idauniq,
                        hearing_base = to01(hearing_loss),
                        vision_base  = to01(vision_overall),
                        frailty_base = to01(frailty)),
            by = "idauniq")

# Checks: same people and events as the Cox models; baseline status equals
# the exposure of each person's first interval (tstart = 0)
first_iv <- tv_cc %>%
  mutate(idauniq = as.character(idauniq)) %>%
  filter(tstart == 0) %>%
  transmute(idauniq, h0 = to01(hearing_lag), v0 = to01(vision_lag), f0 = to01(frailty_lag))
chk <- inner_join(km_base, first_iv, by = "idauniq")
stopifnot(
  "a tv_cc person has no baseline status" =
    !anyNA(km_base[c("hearing_base", "vision_base", "frailty_base")]),
  "KM data and tv_cc have different people" =
    nrow(km_base) == n_distinct(tv_cc$idauniq),
  "KM data and tv_cc have different events" =
    sum(km_base$event) == sum(tv_cc$event),
  "baseline status differs from the first tv_cc interval" =
    all(chk$hearing_base == chk$h0, chk$vision_base == chk$v0, chk$frailty_base == chk$f0)
)
cat("KM data: persons =", nrow(km_base), "| events =", sum(km_base$event),
    "| person-years to the last assessed wave =", round(sum(km_base$t_event)), "\n")
rm(first_iv, chk)

# ---- 1) One plot per exposure --------------------------------------------------
plot_cum_inc <- function(var, labs, legend_title, title, file) {
  d <- km_base %>%
    mutate(group = factor(.data[[var]], levels = c(0, 1), labels = labs))

  # Unadjusted HR for baseline status, and the log-rank test
  ci <- summary(coxph(Surv(t_event, event) ~ group, data = d))$conf.int
  hr_text <- sprintf("Unadjusted HR (95%% CI): %.2f (%.2f–%.2f)",
                     ci[1, "exp(coef)"], ci[1, "lower .95"], ci[1, "upper .95"])
  sd   <- survdiff(Surv(t_event, event) ~ group, data = d)
  p_lr <- pchisq(sd$chisq, df = length(sd$n) - 1, lower.tail = FALSE)
  p_text <- if (p_lr < 0.001) "Log-rank p < 0.001" else sprintf("Log-rank p = %.3f", p_lr)

  fit_km <- surv_fit(Surv(t_event, event) ~ group, data = d)

  p <- ggsurvplot(
    fit_km,
    data           = d,
    fun            = "event",
    conf.int       = TRUE,
    conf.int.style = "ribbon",
    censor         = FALSE,
    risk.table     = TRUE,
    risk.table.col = "strata",
    break.time.by  = 4,
    palette        = c("#00BFC4", "#F8766D"),
    legend.title   = legend_title,
    legend.labs    = labs,
    xlab           = "Follow-up time (years)",
    ylab           = "Cumulative incidence of dementia",
    title          = title
  )
  p$plot <- p$plot +
    annotate("text", x = Inf, y = -Inf,
             label = paste(hr_text, p_text, sep = "\n"),
             hjust = 1.02, vjust = -0.25, size = 4.5) +
    coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +
    theme(plot.margin = margin(10, 20, 25, 10))

  print(p)
  tiff(file.path(KM_OUT_DIR, file),
       width = 8, height = 7, units = "in", res = 300, compression = "lzw")
  print(p)
  dev.off()

  counts <- d %>%
    group_by(group) %>%
    summarise(persons = n(), events = sum(event),
              person_years = round(sum(t_event)), .groups = "drop")
  cat("\n", title, "\n", sep = "")
  print(as.data.frame(counts), row.names = FALSE)
  cat(hr_text, "|", p_text, "\n")

  invisible(list(plot = p, fit = fit_km, counts = counts,
                 HR = ci[1, c("exp(coef)", "lower .95", "upper .95")], p_logrank = p_lr))
}

km_hearing <- plot_cum_inc("hearing_base", c("No hearing loss", "Hearing loss"),
                           "Baseline hearing",
                           "Cumulative Incidence of Dementia by Hearing Status (ELSA)",
                           "KM_hearing_cumincidence_ELSA.tiff")
km_vision  <- plot_cum_inc("vision_base", c("No vision loss", "Vision loss"),
                           "Baseline vision",
                           "Cumulative Incidence of Dementia by Vision Status (ELSA)",
                           "KM_vision_cumincidence_ELSA.tiff")
km_frailty <- plot_cum_inc("frailty_base", c("Non-frail", "Frail"),
                           "Baseline frailty",
                           "Cumulative Incidence of Dementia by Frailty Status (ELSA)",
                           "KM_frailty_cumincidence_ELSA.tiff")

# ---- 2) Save the data and numbers behind the plots -----------------------------
saveRDS(list(data    = km_base,
             hearing = km_hearing[c("fit", "counts", "HR", "p_logrank")],
             vision  = km_vision[c("fit", "counts", "HR", "p_logrank")],
             frailty = km_frailty[c("fit", "counts", "HR", "p_logrank")]),

cat("\nSaved 3 TIFFs to", KM_OUT_DIR, "and KM_cumincidence_ELSA.rds to", results_dir, "\n")
```
